0. FOREWORD

0.1 This Indian Standard was adopted by the Indian Standards Institution on 16 February 1966, after the draft finalized by the Marine Engineering and Shipbuilding Sectional Committee had been approved by the Mechanical Engineering Division Council. 0.2 This standard is one of a series of Indian Standards on cowl ventilators. ' Other standards in the series are: IS IS IS IS Dimensions for oval-head steel cowl Dimensions for circular-head steel Dimensions for accessories for steel Dimensions for mechanical turning ventilators Dimensions for coamings for steel IS : 3277(under preparation) IS : 3278-1966 Dimensions for detachable coaming mesh grids for steel cowl ventilators : : : : 3272-1966 3273-1966 3275-1966 3276-1966 steel cowl ventilators cowl ventilators cowl ventilators arrangements for cowl ventilators covers and wire

0.3 In the preparation of this standard, assistance has been derived from the following standards issued by Association Francaise de Normalisation : NF 546-l 00 : 1951 Manches a air-gtnCralitCs. (Ventilators-general requirements) NF 546-120 : 1951 Manches a air-Gt dtmontable. (Detachable type ventilators) 0.4 For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, the final value, observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test, shall be rounded off in accordance with IS : 2-1960*. The number of significant places retained in the rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard.
*Rules for rounding off numerical values (revise~I).

IS t 3271.1966 1. SCOPE 1.1 This standard deals with the general requirements for steel cowl ventilators with detachable components for sea-going vessels.
2. TERMINOLOGY

2.0 For the purpose of this standard,

the following definition

shall apply. is the internal

2.1 Nominal Size - Nominal size of steel cowl ventilator diameter of the intermediate trunking of the ventilator.

3. DES'CRIPTION
3.1 The ventilator consists of a head (cowl), an intermediate trunking main trunking (coaming) as shown in Fig. 1. The cowl ventilators normally named after the shape of the outlet section of the head. 3.2 The two types of cowl ventilators cowl ventilators, cowl ventilators. are : and and are

a) circular-head

b) oval-head

3.3 The ventilators shall be fabricated by riveting or by welding. In case of welded ventilators, the weld metal should be ground flush. Where riveting is used the rivet heads shall be flush with the beading bar. Finished ventilators should be galvanized or coated with anti-corrosive paint, so as to minimize corrosion due to direct contact with sea water and saline atmosphere. 4. MATERIAL

4.1 The material of steel plates used for construction of various parts of ventilators shall conform to IS : 2062-1962* for welded construction and IS : 1079-19637 or IS : 2062-1062* for riveted construction.
4.2 Tubes used for hand rails shall be YSt 25 heavy quality IS : 1161-1963:. 4.3 Rods used for hand grips shall be made of structural IS : 2062-1962". 4.4 Wire mesh IS : 1568-1960s. used for wire mesh grids conforming to to

steel conforming

shall be in accordance

with

*Specification for structural steel (fusion welding quality). TSpecification for hot rolled carbon steel sheet and strip (revised). $Specification for steel tubes for structural purposes (reuised). �Specification for wire gauge for general purposes. 4

MAINTENANCE 7.1 Ventilator, intermediate trunking and head should be removed periodiThe carrier ring on the main air trunking cally for chipping and repainting. should be cleaned thoroughly and greased. In the case of mechanically operated ventilators, the rollers, the guide pipe, the wheel and pinions should be cleaned thoroughly and greased. 8. DESIGNATION

8.1 The steel cowl ventilators shall be designated by the name, type, the nominal size and number of the standard. Designations shall be as specified in relevant standards.
